description: Phase 1 feature taxonomy mapping GSS variable names to one of {primary_eval, sensitivity_eval, demographic, behavioral, psychological, attitudinal, exclude}. Locked in writing before pipeline runs; will be the OSF pre-registration content for Phase 1b.
design:
Path A* (Path B as primary, Path A as sensitivity, applied to GSS 2024 cross-section, N=3,309):
  - primary_eval: 12 high-variance items, one per construct family. The 4-bin LOO ablation runs against this set.
  - sensitivity_eval: ~118-item Park v2 GSS list (post their 27-item AVP-overlap removal, minus 15 retired/renamed in 2024). Used ONLY for per-item raw-accuracy comparison to Park v2 Table 3. No LOO.
  - demographic / behavioral / psychological / attitudinal: feature pool partitioned into the 4 LOO bins.
  - exclude: utility/meta/derived variables not used in any prompt or eval.

leakage_rules._summary: Direct leakage (same item in features AND target eval) is prohibited. Constructive auto-correlation across related items (e.g., abortion battery, confidence battery) is acknowledged as a methodological limitation, NOT prevented — see limitations in gss_phase1_design.md §8.
leakage_rules.primary_loo_analysis: Declared feature bins MUST be disjoint from primary_eval. Validator enforces this. The LOO conditions drop one full bin at a time; no item is ever both in features and in primary_eval.
leakage_rules.sensitivity_analysis_per_item:
When predicting a sensitivity-eval item X (X ∈ sensitivity_eval), gss_pipeline.py builds the persona prompt from features that EXCLUDE X. Other sensitivity-eval items that happen to live in feature bins MAY remain in the prompt. This is a per-item exclusion rule, not a per-set exclusion rule, because excluding the entire ~118-item sensitivity_eval from features would empty the psychological bin (most psych-relevant GSS items are ALSO in Park's eval list).

GSS auto-correlation across related items (e.g., predicting ABDEFECT when ABNOMORE is in features) IS a real methodological caveat: the contribution of `attitudinal` features to attitude-prediction will be partly inflated by within-domain correlation with other attitude features. See limitations.
leakage_rules.constructive_auto_correlation: Phase 1 estimates feature-category contribution WITHIN GSS-attitude prediction. Attitudinal-feature contribution is partially driven by within-domain auto-correlation (e.g., abortion-battery items predicting each other). Results should NOT be generalized as 'the LLM persona has high human-simulation fidelity' — they speak only to which feature categories most help GSS-attitudinal-item prediction in a single-wave snapshot. BFI personality and behavioral-game prediction are out of scope (Phase 2 will address).

missingness_rule: GSS ballot rotation means not every respondent gets every item. For each (respondent, item), if value is in the missing-codes set MISSING_CODES (defined in gss_loader.py: {-100, -99, -98, -97, -96, -95, -90, -80, -70, -60, -50, -40}) we treat it as absent and EXCLUDE that item from that respondent's feature/eval set for that pass. We do NOT impute. Aggregation rules in gss_phase1_design.md §10 specify how per-respondent metrics are combined into headline numbers under uneven coverage.

primary_eval._note: Path B's 12 curated items. Each from a different construct family to minimize within-eval auto-correlation.

items.scale_text: 1=Strongly agree ... 4=Strongly disagree (mother working doesn't hurt children)

sensitivity_eval._note: Park v2 Table 3 list (after their 27-item AVP-overlap removal). Used for per-item Park comparability only; no LOO. Items overlap with primary_eval (which is intentional — primary_eval is the headline subset).

feature_bins._note: Phase 1 feature pool, partitioned into 4 bins. LOO ablation drops one bin at a time from the persona prompt. Declared bins MUST be disjoint from `primary_eval` (validator enforces). Sensitivity-eval items MAY appear in feature bins; per-item exclusion of the prediction target X happens at runtime in gss_pipeline.py. See top-level `leakage_rules` field for the full rule and constructive-auto-correlation caveat.
feature_bins._resolution_rule: See top-level `leakage_rules` field — declared feature bins are disjoint from primary_eval (validator enforces); sensitivity-eval items MAY appear in feature bins but are excluded per-item when they are the prediction target.

exclude._note: Variables NOT used in any persona prompt or eval. Includes meta variables, weights, derived/computed indices, sampling-specific items.

_audit.2026-05-02: Initial lock post-Bayati: Path A* design, GSS 2024 single-wave snapshot, 3,309 respondents.
_audit.2026-05-05:
Codex audit fixes applied:
  (a) PARTYID removed from `attitudinal` feature bin (it is in primary_eval; declared feature bins are now disjoint from primary_eval).
  (b) `leakage_rules` field rewritten to be self-consistent — declared feature bins disjoint from primary_eval; sensitivity-eval items MAY appear in features with per-item exclusion when predicted.
  (c) Constructive auto-correlation explicitly acknowledged as a methodological caveat (not silently allowed).
  (d) Missingness rule cross-references gss_loader.py MISSING_CODES; aggregation rule cross-references gss_phase1_design.md §10.
_audit.data_source: GSS 2024 cross-section (3,309 respondents, 973 unique variables, downloaded via GSS Data Explorer)
_audit.loader: gss_loader.py — combines 3 batches horizontally into single DataFrame at 3,309 × 973 after dropping repeated YEAR + ID_ identifier columns from batches 2-3.
